title: Storm Runner
location: Spaceport Approach and the Spaceport — the way off Keth'zar
summary: There's a ship called the Storm Runner on the Spaceport apron, and there's a Garrison Commander who'd rather burn it than let it leave. Take the ship. Take the war with you. And if a well-dressed man with cold-metal cologne is on that apron — that's your call.

objectives.text: Break the Spaceport approach. Vehicle combat — the Defense Commander has the outer perimeter.
Reach the apron. The Storm Runner is fueled at the far end — under the Garrison's guns.
The Quartermaster is here in person, brokering the Garrison's resupply. He recognizes you. He has nowhere to run, and he knows it.
Fuel and crew the Storm Runner while the alliance holds the apron.

args.text: Every ally you brought is a gun on that line. Use them.

objectives.text: The Garrison Commander makes a stand on the loading ramp. He won't let the ship leave whole. Prove him wrong.

args.text: Last door off this world. He's standing in it.

objectives.text: Get the Storm Runner off the ground. Whoever's still standing comes with you. Whoever isn't, you carry differently.

_hooks: Act-2 climax — canon L19 Spaceport Approach (Defense Commander mini-boss, vehicle combat) + L20 The Spaceport / 'Escape From Kethzar Prime' (Garrison Commander boss; capture the Storm Runner; ship choice affects Act 3). give-gated on act2.alliance_formed (act2_many_hands) so the ally count earned across Act 2 literally crews the ship. Optional o2_qm pays off the Quartermaster heist (act2_quartermasters_ledger): if the ledger is held, he appears in person for the spare/kill confrontation the expansion (a) promised (sparing → quartermaster.witness, the Act-4 trial prosecutor's witness). act_transition fire hands off to Act 3. The Defense/Garrison Commanders are staged via spawn_boss for the engine's existing boss machine.
_voice: Momentum and cost. The launch line ('whoever isn't, you carry differently') keeps the loss restrained and personal. The Quartermaster confrontation is the only place his civilian menace gets a face — and even then he is bargained with, not boss-fought.
